angle: the object in the machine's name, drawn literally and well
subject: Ants drawn literally: a few hidden-line 3D ants, modelled from ellipsoids with segmented gasters and jointed legs, walking the bright trail between low degree stones in two rows, under one camera.
controls: ants: count, modelled ants on the trail, 1 to 8, nearer ones larger, each easing in from the nest end of the loop.
scent: position, how closely the ants keep to the trail: at 0 they straggle up to a stone's width off it at random headings, at 100 they walk nose to tail on it (≥ 24 px).
fade: count, the dashed old routes between stones: two at 0–30, none at 100.
scale: count + position, the stones per row: 5 at pent to 12 at chrom per octave, closing up along each row.
muted: Muted: the trail drops to the stone grey and the ants stand still.
risks: The ants need pre-drawn variants per heading (a node can't turn out of the screen plane), so 8 ants × several headings is the costliest of the five. At 1:1 the far ants overlap stones and the legs read busy; three weights and hidden-line keep it legible but it's the most cluttered frame. Close in look to theseus' black-with-grey-edge family. The near row runs off both sides of the frame.
